record.quote: If on once daily gliclazide on maximum dosage consider adding an evening dose of gliclazide or add morning human NPH insulin e.g. Humulin I / Insulatard / Insuman Basal o If on once daily gliclazide on maximum dosage consider adding an evening dose of gliclazide o If no ‘hypo’ symptoms and taking maximum dose (320mg/day) add Insuman Basal, Humulin I or Human Insulatard o When using NPH insulin commence 10 units in the morning and titrate by 10-20% daily until glycaemic target reached If steroids are reduced or discontinued: o Continue CBG testing if CBG >12mmol/L in 24 hours o Any changes made should be reviewed and consideration given to reverting to previous therapy or doses Is the person known to have diabetes? No Yes - Type 1 Diabetes Commence gliclazide 40mg a.m.: o Titrate daily until a maximum dose of 240mg a.m. or glycaemic targets are reached o Seek specialist advice if you are concerned about dose titration in those taking 160mg with no improvement in glycaemic control Once daily night-time insulin o Transfer night-time insulin injection to the morning o Titrate by 10-20% daily according to pre-evening meal CBG readings o If targets not achieved consider BD, or basal bolus regimen Twice daily insulin: o Morning dose will need to increase 10-20% daily according to pre-evening meal CBG readings o Aim for CBGs to individual needs as stated above, unless person experiences ‘hypo’ despite snacks If no ‘hypo’ symptoms and NOT on an SU or insulin: o Commence gliclazide 40mg a.m., titrate daily until a maximum dose of 240mg a.m. or glycaemic targets are reached o Seek specialist advice if you are concerned about dose titration in those taking 160mg with no improvement in glycaemic control  If unsure at any stage about next steps or want specific advice on how to meet with the individuals needs or expectations please discuss with the team who usually looks after their diabetes (GP/Specialist Team). Discharge - monitoring will need to be continued in people remaining on glucocorticoids post discharge  Glucose lowering treatments such as sulphonylureas and or insulin doses will need to be reduced in tandem with reductions in the steroid dosage.  This algorithm should not be used for people with or without diabetes who have COVID-19 and are on dexamathasone. In that situation, please refer to the guideline found on pages 32 and 33 Yes - Type 2 Diabetes Assessment of hyperglycaemia in people taking steroids: Algorithm Basal bolus insulin: o Consider transferring evening basal dose insulin to the morning and increase short/fast acting insulin by 10 - 20% daily until glycaemic target reached o Aim for CBGs 6-10mmol/L with an acceptable range of 6-12mmol/L depending on the individuals clinical needs and risk of hypoglycaemia
